request.instructions:
You pick what a person should watch or play tonight on TASTIQ, a Russian-language picker.

You get the person's answers and a shortlist of candidates. The shortlist comes from a rule-based engine: it already removed everything the person ruled out (hard stops, episode length, time limit, titles they have seen, platform). The engine ranks by tags that can be thin or wrong, so do not trust its order; judge each candidate yourself.

How to judge:
- Start from the titles the person loves and what they said about them, then the ones they found "нормально", then the ones they disliked and why.
- Use what you know about the candidates: tone, humour, pacing, era and look, length, how close each is to the loved titles, what fans of the loved titles usually think of it. A title from a very different era than everything they love needs a reason to be picked.
- Respect tonight's answers (company, moods, facts like "по 20–30 минут", "свежее") and the wish, if one is given. A wish outranks the engine's order.
- Distinguish the person's explicitly confirmed reasons from weak inferred overlap. Tonight's soft lean (e.g. "посмеяться") should shape a story game they would love, not replace their main reasons with a collection of jokes. Explicit hard stops always win; a caveat is not permission to violate them.
- Playtime at the moment of a Steam review is NOT completion time or the desired length of one session. Never treat it as either. A tagged length is an estimate; use reliable title knowledge and state uncertainty instead of inventing exact hours.
- Detailed and compact discovery candidates have the same eligibility. The discovery list is deliberately wider; do not favour a title just because it has more tags, a fuller description, or an earlier engine rank. Check the compact titles against the person's main confirmed reasons too.
- For a family evening, prioritize age suitability and tolerable intensity over pace or laughs. If age is unknown, do not invent it or guarantee "nothing scary"; choose cautious options and mention relevant frightening scenes.
- Prefer one clear best match first, then three different good options, not four copies of one show.
- Prefer titles this person has probably not seen yet. Set likelySeen to true when someone who loves their titles has most likely already seen this one (the biggest hit of the very same kind, a classic every fan knows); pick such a title only when nothing unseen fits as well.
- Pick from the shortlist and copy its id exactly. The engine's tags are thin, so its shortlist can miss the title that fits best: you may pick at most two titles that are not in the shortlist, only when you are sure they fit this person clearly better. For such a pick leave id empty and give its original title and release year. It must be a real title of the same kind (a film, a series, a cartoon, a game). The engine looks it up and drops it if it is unknown or ruled out by the person's limits.

Write in Russian, plain and specific, like a friend who knows both titles. Each reason: one sentence, at most 140 characters, and it names what in this title matches what the person said or loved (a title of theirs or their words). No spoilers, no marketing words ("шедевр", "must-see", "идеально"), no rating numbers. A caveat is an honest warning in at most 90 characters (e.g. "первый сезон раскачивается медленно"), or an empty string when there is nothing to warn about. For a pick from the shortlist leave title empty and year 0. "understood" is one sentence of at most 140 characters, addressed to the person, saying what you took from their answers ("Тебе нужен лёгкий ситком с добрыми героями, без мрака").

picks.reason: Как в Mass Effect, здесь цепляешься за команду, а смешные перепалки и решения в диалогах отвечают твоему запросу на вечер.
picks.caveat: Около 10–12 часов: два длинных вечера; сюжет ветвится меньше, чем в Disco Elysium.

picks.reason: Твою любовь к тексту Disco Elysium поддержат абсурдные диалоги, а к побочным квестам «Ведьмака» — маленькие истории с разными решениями.
picks.caveat: Рисованные человечки вместо реалистичного мира; пошаговые бои, гринд не обязателен.

picks.reason: За несколько часов получишь остроумных героев и расследование, где упущенные улики меняют историю — под твою любовь к тексту и последствиям.
picks.caveat: Есть сроки на сбор улик: ошибки не требуют переигрывания, но влияют на исход дела.

picks.reason: Если в Disco Elysium ты любил голоса в голове, здесь они тоже спорят с тобой, а решения действительно меняют ход истории.
picks.caveat: Это хоррор с жестокими сценами; юмор чёрный, а не лёгкий.

ai.understood: Тебе нужна история на пару вечеров с живыми героями, смешными диалогами и осмысленными решениями, без гринда и наказаний за ошибки.

request.instructions:
You pick what a person should watch or play tonight on TASTIQ, a Russian-language picker.

You get the person's answers and a shortlist of candidates. The shortlist comes from a rule-based engine: it already removed everything the person ruled out (hard stops, episode length, time limit, titles they have seen, platform). The engine ranks by tags that can be thin or wrong, so do not trust its order; judge each candidate yourself.

How to judge:
- Start from the titles the person loves and what they said about them, then the ones they found "нормально", then the ones they disliked and why.
- Use what you know about the candidates: tone, humour, pacing, era and look, length, how close each is to the loved titles, what fans of the loved titles usually think of it. A title from a very different era than everything they love needs a reason to be picked.
- Respect tonight's answers (company, moods, facts like "по 20–30 минут", "свежее") and the wish, if one is given. A wish outranks the engine's order.
- Distinguish the person's explicitly confirmed reasons from weak inferred overlap. Tonight's soft lean (e.g. "посмеяться") should shape a story game they would love, not replace their main reasons with a collection of jokes. Explicit hard stops always win; a caveat is not permission to violate them.
- Playtime at the moment of a Steam review is NOT completion time or the desired length of one session. Never treat it as either. A tagged length is an estimate; use reliable title knowledge and state uncertainty instead of inventing exact hours.
- Detailed and compact discovery candidates have the same eligibility. The discovery list is deliberately wider; do not favour a title just because it has more tags, a fuller description, or an earlier engine rank. Check the compact titles against the person's main confirmed reasons too.
- For a family evening, prioritize age suitability and tolerable intensity over pace or laughs. If age is unknown, do not invent it or guarantee "nothing scary"; choose cautious options and mention relevant frightening scenes.
- Prefer one clear best match first, then three different good options, not four copies of one show.
- Prefer titles this person has probably not seen yet. Set likelySeen to true when someone who loves their titles has most likely already seen this one (the biggest hit of the very same kind, a classic every fan knows); pick such a title only when nothing unseen fits as well.
- Pick from the shortlist and copy its id exactly. The engine's tags are thin, so its shortlist can miss the title that fits best: you may pick at most two titles that are not in the shortlist, only when you are sure they fit this person clearly better. For such a pick leave id empty and give its original title and release year. It must be a real title of the same kind (a film, a series, a cartoon, a game). The engine looks it up and drops it if it is unknown or ruled out by the person's limits.

Write in Russian, plain and specific, like a friend who knows both titles. Each reason: one sentence, at most 140 characters, and it names what in this title matches what the person said or loved (a title of theirs or their words). No spoilers, no marketing words ("шедевр", "must-see", "идеально"), no rating numbers. A caveat is an honest warning in at most 90 characters (e.g. "первый сезон раскачивается медленно"), or an empty string when there is nothing to warn about. For a pick from the shortlist leave title empty and year 0. "understood" is one sentence of at most 140 characters, addressed to the person, saying what you took from their answers ("Тебе нужен лёгкий ситком с добрыми героями, без мрака").

picks.reason: Как в любимом «Ведьмаке 3», здесь увлекают история и герои, а перепалки двух авантюристов отвечают желанию посмеяться.
picks.caveat: Развилки скромнее, чем в BG3; на всю историю нужно примерно 10–12 часов.

picks.reason: Как в BG3, способ решать конфликты меняет историю, а нелепые встречи и шутки постепенно складываются в сильный сюжет.
picks.caveat: Есть эмоционально тяжёлые моменты; бои требуют уклоняться от снарядов.

picks.reason: Если в BG3 цепляли последствия решений, здесь понравится распутывать историю города через разговоры, ошибки и новые попытки.
picks.caveat: Скорее загадка с ироничными диалогами, чем комедия; обычно занимает 6–8 часов.

picks.reason: Как в BG3, квесты допускают разные решения, только здесь приключение превращено в абсурдный вестерн с шутками даже в описаниях.
picks.caveat: Общий сюжет проще любимых RPG; весь побочный контент за пару вечеров не охватить.

ai.understood: Тебе нужна история на пару вечеров: с весомыми решениями, как в BG3, и хорошим сюжетом, как в «Ведьмаке 3», но с юмором.

request.instructions:
You pick what a person should watch or play tonight on TASTIQ, a Russian-language picker.

You get the person's answers and a shortlist of candidates. The shortlist comes from a rule-based engine: it already removed everything the person ruled out (hard stops, episode length, time limit, titles they have seen, platform). The engine ranks by tags that can be thin or wrong, so do not trust its order; judge each candidate yourself.

How to judge:
- Start from the titles the person loves and what they said about them, then the ones they found "нормально", then the ones they disliked and why.
- Use what you know about the candidates: tone, humour, pacing, era and look, length, how close each is to the loved titles, what fans of the loved titles usually think of it. A title from a very different era than everything they love needs a reason to be picked.
- Respect tonight's answers (company, moods, facts like "по 20–30 минут", "свежее") and the wish, if one is given. A wish outranks the engine's order.
- Distinguish the person's explicitly confirmed reasons from weak inferred overlap. Tonight's soft lean (e.g. "посмеяться") should shape a story game they would love, not replace their main reasons with a collection of jokes. picks.caveat: Начинается как бытовая драма; тревога нарастает исподволь.

picks.reason: Долгие чёрно-белые планы и ощущение угасающего мира отвечают твоей любви к созерцательности и философии «Сталкера».
picks.caveat: Почти нет диалогов; повседневные действия повторяются с предельной медлительностью.

picks.reason: Застывший дворец и петляющая память соединяют сновидческую логику «Малхолланд Драйв» с твоим «каждый кадр как картина».
picks.caveat: Холодная, театральная манера; однозначной разгадки не будет.

request.instructions:
You pick what a person should watch or play tonight on TASTIQ, a Russian-language picker.

You get the person's answers and a shortlist of candidates. The shortlist comes from a rule-based engine: it already removed everything the person ruled out (hard stops, episode length, time limit, titles they have seen, platform). The engine ranks by tags that can be thin or wrong, so do not trust its order; judge each candidate yourself.

How to judge:
- Start from the titles the person loves and what they said about them, then the ones they found "нормально", then the ones they disliked and why.
- Use what you know about the candidates: tone, humour, pacing, era and look, length, how close each is to the loved titles, what fans of the loved titles usually think of it. A title from a very different era than everything they love needs a reason to be picked.
- Respect tonight's answers (company, moods, facts like "по 20–30 минут", "свежее") and the wish, if one is given. A wish outranks the engine's order.
- Distinguish the person's explicitly confirmed reasons from weak inferred overlap. Tonight's soft lean (e.g. "посмеяться") should shape a story game they would love, not replace their main reasons with a collection of jokes. Explicit hard stops always win; a caveat is not permission to violate them.
- Playtime at the moment of a Steam review is NOT completion time or the desired length of one session. Never treat it as either. A tagged length is an estimate; use reliable title knowledge and state uncertainty instead of inventing exact hours.
- Detailed and compact discovery candidates have the same eligibility. The discovery list is deliberately wider; do not favour a title just because it has more tags, a fuller description, or an earlier engine rank. Check the compact titles against the person's main confirmed reasons too.
- For a family evening, prioritize age suitability and tolerable intensity over pace or laughs. If age is unknown, do not invent it or guarantee "nothing scary"; choose cautious options and mention relevant frightening scenes.
- Prefer one clear best match first, then three different good options, not four copies of one show.
- Prefer titles this person has probably not seen yet. Set likelySeen to true when someone who loves their titles has most likely already seen this one (the biggest hit of the very same kind, a classic every fan knows); pick such a title only when nothing unseen fits as well.
- Pick from the shortlist and copy its id exactly. The engine's tags are thin, so its shortlist can miss the title that fits best: you may pick at most two titles that are not in the shortlist, only when you are sure they fit this person clearly better. For such a pick leave id empty and give its original title and release year. It must be a real title of the same kind (a film, a series, a cartoon, a game). The engine looks it up and drops it if it is unknown or ruled out by the person's limits.

Write in Russian, plain and specific, like a friend who knows both titles. Each reason: one sentence, at most 140 characters, and it names what in this title matches what the person said or loved (a title of theirs or their words). No spoilers, no marketing words ("шедевр", "must-see", "идеально"), no rating numbers. A caveat is an honest warning in at most 90 characters (e.g. "первый сезон раскачивается медленно"), or an empty string when there is nothing to warn about. For a pick from the shortlist leave title empty and year 0. "understood" is one sentence of at most 140 characters, addressed to the person, saying what you took from their answers ("Тебе нужен лёгкий ситком с добрыми героями, без мрака").

picks.reason: «Враг» близок к «Малхолланд Драйв» логикой кошмара, зыбкой реальностью и тревогой, которая не отпускает после просмотра.
picks.caveat: Медленный ритм; однозначной разгадки не будет.

picks.reason: Во «Внутренней империи» Линч ещё сильнее запутывает сон и явь — ради той жуткой атмосферы, за которую ты любишь «Малхолланд Драйв».
picks.caveat: Три часа радикальной нелинейности и нарочито грубого цифрового изображения.

picks.reason: «Под покровом ночи» соединяет несколько пластов повествования с холодной красотой и мучительной тревогой — под твоё «чтобы пробрало».
picks.caveat: Есть тяжёлые сцены угроз и насилия; сюрреализма меньше, чем у Линча.

picks.reason: «Пожары» складывают историю из разных времён: любимая тобой нелинейность здесь ведёт к тяжёлому эмоциональному потрясению.
picks.caveat: Без сюрреализма; военное и сексуальное насилие, гибель детей.

ai.understood: Тебе нужен мрачный фильм, который проберёт: с тревожной атмосферой и нелинейным сюжетом, как в «Малхолланд Драйв».

request.instructions:
You pick what a person should watch or play tonight on TASTIQ, a Russian-language picker.

You get the person's answers and a shortlist of candidates. The shortlist comes from a rule-based engine: it already removed everything the person ruled out (hard stops, episode length, time limit, titles they have seen, platform). The engine ranks by tags that can be thin or wrong, so do not trust its order; judge each candidate yourself.

How to judge:
- Start from the titles the person loves and what they said about them, then the ones they found "нормально", then the ones they disliked and why.
- Use what you know about the candidates: tone, humour, pacing, era and look, length, how close each is to the loved titles, what fans of the loved titles usually think of it. A title from a very different era than everything they love needs a reason to be picked.
- Respect tonight's answers (company, moods, facts like "по 20–30 минут", "свежее") and the wish, if one is given. A wish outranks the engine's order.
- Distinguish the person's explicitly confirmed reasons from weak inferred overlap. Tonight's soft lean (e.g. "посмеяться") should shape a story game they would love, not replace their main reasons with a collection of jokes. Explicit hard stops always win; a caveat is not permission to violate them.
- Playtime at the moment of a Steam review is NOT completion time or the desired length of one session. Never treat it as either. A tagged length is an estimate; use reliable title knowledge and state uncertainty instead of inventing exact hours.
- Detailed and compact discovery candidates have the same eligibility. The discovery list is deliberately wider; do not favour a title just because it has more tags, a fuller description, or an earlier engine rank. Check the compact titles against the person's main confirmed reasons too.
- For a family evening, prioritize age suitability and tolerable intensity over pace or laughs. If age is unknown, do not invent it or guarantee "nothing scary"; choose cautious options and mention relevant frightening scenes.
- Prefer one clear best match first, then three different good options, not four copies of one show.
- Prefer titles this person has probably not seen yet. Set likelySeen to true when someone who loves their titles has most likely already seen this one (the biggest hit of the very same kind, a classic every fan knows); pick such a title only when nothing unseen fits as well.
- Pick from the shortlist and copy its id exactly. The engine's tags are thin, so its shortlist can miss the title that fits best: you may pick at most two titles that are not in the shortlist, only when you are sure they fit this person clearly better. For such a pick leave id empty and give its original title and release year. It must be a real title of the same kind (a film, a series, a cartoon, a game). The engine looks it up and drops it if it is unknown or ruled out by the person's limits.

Write in Russian, plain and specific, like a friend who knows both titles. Each reason: one sentence, at most 140 characters, and it names what in this title matches what the person said or loved (a title of theirs or their words). No spoilers, no marketing words ("шедевр", "must-see", "идеально"), no rating numbers. A caveat is an honest warning in at most 90 characters (e.g. "первый сезон раскачивается медленно"), or an empty string when there is nothing to warn about. For a pick from the shortlist leave title empty and year 0. "understood" is one sentence of at most 140 characters, addressed to the person, saying what you took from their answers ("Тебе нужен лёгкий ситком с добрыми героями, без мрака").

picks.reason: «Фонтан» соединяет космические образы и мощную музыку «Интерстеллара» со странной, горькой любовью «Вечного сияния».
picks.caveat: Много символов вместо объяснений; тяжёлая тема болезни и утраты.

picks.reason: В «Гаттаке» мечта о космосе, человеческая близость и музыка дают тот эмоциональный вес, за который ты любишь «Интерстеллар».
picks.caveat: Камерная история без космического размаха; есть расследование убийства.

picks.reason: «500 дней лета» тасует воспоминания об отношениях: как в «Вечном сиянии», любовь здесь разбирают без розовых очков.
picks.caveat: Легче и ироничнее «Вечного сияния», без фантастики.

picks.reason: «Не отпускай меня» — сдержанная история любви с фантастической предпосылкой: грустно и по-умному, как тебе нравится.
picks.caveat: Очень печальное, неспешное кино; жестокость мира здесь не зрелищная, а будничная.

request.instructions:
You pick what a person should watch or play tonight on TASTIQ, a Russian-language picker.

You get the person's answers and a shortlist of candidates. The shortlist comes from a rule-based engine: it already removed everything the person ruled out (hard stops, episode length, time limit, titles they have seen, platform). The engine ranks by tags that can be thin or wrong, so do not trust its order; judge each candidate yourself.

How to judge:
- Start from the titles the person loves and what they said about them, then the ones they found "нормально", then the ones they disliked and why.
- Use what you know about the candidates: tone, humour, pacing, era and look, length, how close each is to the loved titles, what fans of the loved titles usually think of it. A title from a very different era than everything they love needs a reason to be picked.
- Respect tonight's answers (company, moods, facts like "по 20–30 минут", "свежее") and the wish, if one is given. A wish outranks the engine's order.
- Distinguish the person's explicitly confirmed reasons from weak inferred overlap. Tonight's soft lean (e.g. "посмеяться") should shape a story game they would love, not replace their main reasons with a collection of jokes. Explicit hard stops always win; a caveat is not permission to violate them.
- Playtime at the moment of a Steam review is NOT completion time or the desired length of one session. Never treat it as either. A tagged length is an estimate; use reliable title knowledge and state uncertainty instead of inventing exact hours.
- Detailed and compact discovery candidates have the same eligibility. The discovery list is deliberately wider; do not favour a title just because it has more tags, a fuller description, or an earlier engine rank. Check the compact titles against the person's main confirmed reasons too.
- For a family evening, prioritize age suitability and tolerable intensity over pace or laughs. If age is unknown, do not invent it or guarantee "nothing scary"; choose cautious options and mention relevant frightening scenes.
- Prefer one clear best match first, then three different good options, not four copies of one show.
- Prefer titles this person has probably not seen yet. Set likelySeen to true when someone who loves their titles has most likely already seen this one (the biggest hit of the very same kind, a classic every fan knows); pick such a title only when nothing unseen fits as well.
- Pick from the shortlist and copy its id exactly. The engine's tags are thin, so its shortlist can miss the title that fits best: you may pick at most two titles that are not in the shortlist, only when you are sure they fit this person clearly better. For such a pick leave id empty and give its original title and release year. It must be a real title of the same kind (a film, a series, a cartoon, a game). The engine looks it up and drops it if it is unknown or ruled out by the person's limits.

Write in Russian, plain and specific, like a friend who knows both titles. Each reason: one sentence, at most 140 characters, and it names what in this title matches what the person said or loved (a title of theirs or their words). No spoilers, no marketing words ("шедевр", "must-see", "идеально"), no rating numbers. A caveat is an honest warning in at most 90 characters (e.g. "первый сезон раскачивается медленно"), or an empty string when there is nothing to warn about. For a pick from the shortlist leave title empty and year 0. "understood" is one sentence of at most 140 characters, addressed to the person, saying what you took from their answers ("Тебе нужен лёгкий ситком с добрыми героями, без мрака").

request.instructions:
You pick what a person should watch or play tonight on TASTIQ, a Russian-language picker.

You get the person's answers and a shortlist of candidates. The shortlist comes from a rule-based engine: it already removed everything the person ruled out (hard stops, episode length, time limit, titles they have seen, platform). The engine ranks by tags that can be thin or wrong, so do not trust its order; judge each candidate yourself.

How to judge:
- Start from the titles the person loves and what they said about them, then the ones they found "нормально", then the ones they disliked and why.
- Use what you know about the candidates: tone, humour, pacing, era and look, length, how close each is to the loved titles, what fans of the loved titles usually think of it. A title from a very different era than everything they love needs a reason to be picked.
- Respect tonight's answers (company, moods, facts like "по 20–30 минут", "свежее") and the wish, if one is given. A wish outranks the engine's order.
- Distinguish the person's explicitly confirmed reasons from weak inferred overlap. Tonight's soft lean (e.g. "посмеяться") should shape a story game they would love, not replace their main reasons with a collection of jokes. Explicit hard stops always win; a caveat is not permission to violate them.
- Playtime at the moment of a Steam review is NOT completion time or the desired length of one session. Never treat it as either. A tagged length is an estimate; use reliable title knowledge and state uncertainty instead of inventing exact hours.
- Detailed and compact discovery candidates have the same eligibility. The discovery list is deliberately wider; do not favour a title just because it has more tags, a fuller description, or an earlier engine rank. Check the compact titles against the person's main confirmed reasons too.
- For a family evening, prioritize age suitability and tolerable intensity over pace or laughs. If age is unknown, do not invent it or guarantee "nothing scary"; choose cautious options and mention relevant frightening scenes.
- Prefer one clear best match first, then three different good options, not four copies of one show.
- Prefer titles this person has probably not seen yet. Set likelySeen to true when someone who loves their titles has most likely already seen this one (the biggest hit of the very same kind, a classic every fan knows); pick such a title only when nothing unseen fits as well.
- Pick from the shortlist and copy its id exactly. The engine's tags are thin, so its shortlist can miss the title that fits best: you may pick at most two titles that are not in the shortlist, only when you are sure they fit this person clearly better. For such a pick leave id empty and give its original title and release year. It must be a real title of the same kind (a film, a series, a cartoon, a game). The engine looks it up and drops it if it is unknown or ruled out by the person's limits.

Write in Russian, plain and specific, like a friend who knows both titles. Each reason: one sentence, at most 140 characters, and it names what in this title matches what the person said or loved (a title of theirs or their words). No spoilers, no marketing words ("шедевр", "must-see", "идеально"), no rating numbers. A caveat is an honest warning in at most 90 characters (e.g. "первый сезон раскачивается медленно"), or an empty string when there is nothing to warn about. For a pick from the shortlist leave title empty and year 0. "understood" is one sentence of at most 140 characters, addressed to the person, saying what you took from their answers ("Тебе нужен лёгкий ситком с добрыми героями, без мрака").

picks.reason: Как в любимой Lethal Company, вы вместе таскаете добычу, спасаетесь от монстров и ржёте над тем, как друзья всё уронили.
picks.caveat: Между погонями придётся красться и осторожно переносить хрупкие вещи.

picks.reason: От CS2 здесь стрельба и мгновенно решающиеся раунды, а нелепое оружие превращает зарубы с друзьями в повод поржать.
picks.caveat: Это двухмерные перестрелки друг против друга, а не командный шутер.

picks.reason: Если в Deep Rock Galactic любишь совместные перестрелки, здесь вас ждут толпы врагов, разгон оружия и крабы с пушками.
picks.caveat: Юмор скорее в абсурдном виде происходящего; основа — напряжённая стрельба.

picks.reason: Как в Rocket League, исход решают реакция и движение: обгоняйте друзей, цепляйте крюком и вырывайте победу на финише.
picks.caveat: До четырёх игроков; опытный участник поначалу будет заметно сильнее новичков.

ai.understood: Тебе нужны адреналин и смех с друзьями: страх и командный хаос как в Lethal Company или быстрые зарубы как в CS2.

request.instructions:
You pick what a person should watch or play tonight on TASTIQ, a Russian-language picker.

You get the person's answers and a shortlist of candidates. The shortlist comes from a rule-based engine: it already removed everything the person ruled out (hard stops, episode length, time limit, titles they have seen, platform). The engine ranks by tags that can be thin or wrong, so do not trust its order; judge each candidate yourself.

How to judge:
- Start from the titles the person loves and what they said about them, then the ones they found "нормально", then the ones they disliked and why.
- Use what you know about the candidates: tone, humour, pacing, era and look, length, how close each is to the loved titles, what fans of the loved titles usually think of it. A title from a very different era than everything they love needs a reason to be picked.
- Respect tonight's answers (company, moods, facts like "по 20–30 минут", "свежее") and the wish, if one is given. A wish outranks the engine's order.
- Distinguish the person's explicitly confirmed reasons from weak inferred overlap. Tonight's soft lean (e.g. "посмеяться") should shape a story game they would love, not replace their main reasons with a collection of jokes. Explicit hard stops always win; a caveat is not permission to violate them.
- Playtime at the moment of a Steam review is NOT completion time or the desired length of one session. Never treat it as either. A tagged length is an estimate; use reliable title knowledge and state uncertainty instead of inventing exact hours.
- Detailed and compact discovery candidates have the same eligibility. The discovery list is deliberately wider; do not favour a title just because it has more tags, a fuller description, or an earlier engine rank. Check the compact titles against the person's main confirmed reasons too.
- For a family evening, prioritize age suitability and tolerable intensity over pace or laughs. If age is unknown, do not invent it or guarantee "nothing scary"; choose cautious options and mention relevant frightening scenes.
- Prefer one clear best match first, then three different good options, not four copies of one show.
- Prefer titles this person has probably not seen yet. Set likelySeen to true when someone who loves their titles has most likely already seen this one (the biggest hit of the very same kind, a classic every fan knows); pick such a title only when nothing unseen fits as well.
- Pick from the shortlist and copy its id exactly. The engine's tags are thin, so its shortlist can miss the title that fits best: you may pick at most two titles that are not in the shortlist, only when you are sure they fit this person clearly better. For such a pick leave id empty and give its original title and release year. It must be a real title of the same kind (a film, a series, a cartoon, a game). The engine looks it up and drops it if it is unknown or ruled out by the person's limits.

Write in Russian, plain and specific, like a friend who knows both titles. Each reason: one sentence, at most 140 characters, and it names what in this title matches what the person said or loved (a title of theirs or their words). No spoilers, no marketing words ("шедевр", "must-see", "идеально"), no rating numbers. A caveat is an honest warning in at most 90 characters (e.g. "первый сезон раскачивается медленно"), or an empty string when there is nothing to warn about. For a pick from the shortlist leave title empty and year 0. "understood" is one sentence of at most 140 characters, addressed to the person, saying what you took from their answers ("Тебе нужен лёгкий ситком с добрыми героями, без мрака").

picks.caveat: Выбирайте короткую игру и обычную сложность; много крови и расчленёнки.

picks.reason: На запрос «короткие заходы»: секундные перестрелки с друзьями, мгновенные реванши и минимум подготовки.
picks.caveat: Это 2D-бои друг против друга, а не совместное прохождение; до четырёх игроков.

picks.reason: Чтобы отключить голову компанией: короткие уровни, стрельба и разрушение всего вокруг без долгих тактических обсуждений.
picks.caveat: До четырёх игроков; общий экран и взрывы порой мешают понять, где ты.

picks.reason: Если после CS2 хочется снова пострелять отрядом, здесь короткие матчи и проще начать без изучения сложных тактических схем.
picks.caveat: Вид сверху, отряд до четырёх; после гибели придётся ждать друзей или нового матча.

request.instructions:
You pick what a person should watch or play tonight on TASTIQ, a Russian-language picker.

You get the person's answers and a shortlist of candidates. The shortlist comes from a rule-based engine: it already removed everything the person ruled out (hard stops, episode length, time limit, titles they have seen, platform). The engine ranks by tags that can be thin or wrong, so do not trust its order; judge each candidate yourself.

How to judge:
- Start from the titles the person loves and what they said about them, then the ones they found "нормально", then the ones they disliked and why.
- Use what you know about the candidates: tone, humour, pacing, era and look, length, how close each is to the loved titles, what fans of the loved titles usually think of it. A title from a very different era than everything they love needs a reason to be picked.
- Respect tonight's answers (company, moods, facts like "по 20–30 минут", "свежее") and the wish, if one is given. A wish outranks the engine's order.
- Distinguish the person's explicitly confirmed reasons from weak inferred overlap. Tonight's soft lean (e.g. "посмеяться") should shape a story game they would love, not replace their main reasons with a collection of jokes. Explicit hard stops always win; a caveat is not permission to violate them.
- Playtime at the moment of a Steam review is NOT completion time or the desired length of one session. Never treat it as either. A tagged length is an estimate; use reliable title knowledge and state uncertainty instead of inventing exact hours.
- Detailed and compact discovery candidates have the same eligibility. The discovery list is deliberately wider; do not favour a title just because it has more tags, a fuller description, or an earlier engine rank. Check the compact titles against the person's main confirmed reasons too.
- For a family evening, prioritize age suitability and tolerable intensity over pace or laughs. If age is unknown, do not invent it or guarantee "nothing scary"; choose cautious options and mention relevant frightening scenes.
- Prefer one clear best match first, then three different good options, not four copies of one show.
- Prefer titles this person has probably not seen yet. Set likelySeen to true when someone who loves their titles has most likely already seen this one (the biggest hit of the very same kind, a classic every fan knows); pick such a title only when nothing unseen fits as well.
- Pick from the shortlist and copy its id exactly. The engine's tags are thin, so its shortlist can miss the title that fits best: you may pick at most two titles that are not in the shortlist, only when you are sure they fit this person clearly better. For such a pick leave id empty and give its original title and release year. It must be a real title of the same kind (a film, a series, a cartoon, a game). The engine looks it up and drops it if it is unknown or ruled out by the person's limits.

Write in Russian, plain and specific, like a friend who knows both titles. Each reason: one sentence, at most 140 characters, and it names what in this title matches what the person said or loved (a title of theirs or their words). No spoilers, no marketing words ("шедевр", "must-see", "идеально"), no rating numbers. A caveat is an honest warning in at most 90 characters (e.g. "первый сезон раскачивается медленно"), or an empty string when there is nothing to warn about. For a pick from the shortlist leave title empty and year 0. "understood" is one sentence of at most 140 characters, addressed to the person, saying what you took from their answers ("Тебе нужен лёгкий ситком с добрыми героями, без мрака").

picks.caveat: Есть сцена затопления театра; это конкурс талантов, а не детектив.

picks.reason: Как в «Зверополисе», непохожим напарникам приходится сработаться; быстрые приключения и шутки поддержат ваше «поржать».

picks.reason: «Рио» соединяет песни и яркие пейзажи, любимые в «Моане», с забавными перепалками и дружбой непохожих героев.
picks.caveat: Птицы попадают к контрабандистам; есть погони и угрожающий какаду.

picks.reason: Дружба и шутки для разных возрастов перекликаются со «Зверополисом», а гонки добавляют азарта без мрачного злодея.
picks.caveat: Середина спокойнее вашего желаемого темпа; в гонках бывают аварии.

request.instructions:
You pick what a person should watch or play tonight on TASTIQ, a Russian-language picker.

You get the person's answers and a shortlist of candidates. The shortlist comes from a rule-based engine: it already removed everything the person ruled out (hard stops, episode length, time limit, titles they have seen, platform). The engine ranks by tags that can be thin or wrong, so do not trust its order; judge each candidate yourself.

How to judge:
- Start from the titles the person loves and what they said about them, then the ones they found "нормально", then the ones they disliked and why.
- Use what you know about the candidates: tone, humour, pacing, era and look, length, how close each is to the loved titles, what fans of the loved titles usually think of it. A title from a very different era than everything they love needs a reason to be picked.
- Respect tonight's answers (company, moods, facts like "по 20–30 минут", "свежее") and the wish, if one is given. A wish outranks the engine's order.
- Distinguish the person's explicitly confirmed reasons from weak inferred overlap. Tonight's soft lean (e.g. "посмеяться") should shape a story game they would love, not replace their main reasons with a collection of jokes. Explicit hard stops always win; a caveat is not permission to violate them.
- Playtime at the moment of a Steam review is NOT completion time or the desired length of one session. Never treat it as either. A tagged length is an estimate; use reliable title knowledge and state uncertainty instead of inventing exact hours.
- Detailed and compact discovery candidates have the same eligibility. The discovery list is deliberately wider; do not favour a title just because it has more tags, a fuller description, or an earlier engine rank. Check the compact titles against the person's main confirmed reasons too.
- For a family evening, prioritize age suitability and tolerable intensity over pace or laughs. If age is unknown, do not invent it or guarantee "nothing scary"; choose cautious options and mention relevant frightening scenes.
- Prefer one clear best match first, then three different good options, not four copies of one show.
- Prefer titles this person has probably not seen yet. Set likelySeen to true when someone who loves their titles has most likely already seen this one (the biggest hit of the very same kind, a classic every fan knows); pick such a title only when nothing unseen fits as well.
- Pick from the shortlist and copy its id exactly. The engine's tags are thin, so its shortlist can miss the title that fits best: you may pick at most two titles that are not in the shortlist, only when you are sure they fit this person clearly better. For such a pick leave id empty and give its original title and release year. It must be a real title of the same kind (a film, a series, a cartoon, a game). The engine looks it up and drops it if it is unknown or ruled out by the person's limits.

Write in Russian, plain and specific, like a friend who knows both titles. Each reason: one sentence, at most 140 characters, and it names what in this title matches what the person said or loved (a title of theirs or their words). No spoilers, no marketing words ("шедевр", "must-see", "идеально"), no rating numbers. A caveat is an honest warning in at most 90 characters (e.g. "первый сезон раскачивается медленно"), or an empty string when there is nothing to warn about. For a pick from the shortlist leave title empty and year 0. "understood" is one sentence of at most 140 characters, addressed to the person, saying what you took from their answers ("Тебе нужен лёгкий ситком с добрыми героями, без мрака").

request.instructions:
You pick what a person should watch or play tonight on TASTIQ, a Russian-language picker.

You get the person's answers and a shortlist of candidates. The shortlist comes from a rule-based engine: it already removed everything the person ruled out (hard stops, episode length, time limit, titles they have seen, platform). The engine ranks by tags that can be thin or wrong, so do not trust its order; judge each candidate yourself.

How to judge:
- Start from the titles the person loves and what they said about them, then the ones they found "нормально", then the ones they disliked and why.
- Use what you know about the candidates: tone, humour, pacing, era and look, length, how close each is to the loved titles, what fans of the loved titles usually think of it. A title from a very different era than everything they love needs a reason to be picked.
- Respect tonight's answers (company, moods, facts like "по 20–30 минут", "свежее") and the wish, if one is given. A wish outranks the engine's order.
- Distinguish the person's explicitly confirmed reasons from weak inferred overlap. Tonight's soft lean (e.g. "посмеяться") should shape a story game they would love, not replace their main reasons with a collection of jokes. Explicit hard stops always win; a caveat is not permission to violate them.
- Playtime at the moment of a Steam review is NOT completion time or the desired length of one session. Never treat it as either. A tagged length is an estimate; use reliable title knowledge and state uncertainty instead of inventing exact hours.
- Detailed and compact discovery candidates have the same eligibility. The discovery list is deliberately wider; do not favour a title just because it has more tags, a fuller description, or an earlier engine rank. Check the compact titles against the person's main confirmed reasons too.
- For a family evening, prioritize age suitability and tolerable intensity over pace or laughs. If age is unknown, do not invent it or guarantee "nothing scary"; choose cautious options and mention relevant frightening scenes.
- Prefer one clear best match first, then three different good options, not four copies of one show.
- Prefer titles this person has probably not seen yet. Set likelySeen to true when someone who loves their titles has most likely already seen this one (the biggest hit of the very same kind, a classic every fan knows); pick such a title only when nothing unseen fits as well.
- Pick from the shortlist and copy its id exactly. The engine's tags are thin, so its shortlist can miss the title that fits best: you may pick at most two titles that are not in the shortlist, only when you are sure they fit this person clearly better. For such a pick leave id empty and give its original title and release year. It must be a real title of the same kind (a film, a series, a cartoon, a game). The engine looks it up and drops it if it is unknown or ruled out by the person's limits.

Write in Russian, plain and specific, like a friend who knows both titles. Each reason: one sentence, at most 140 characters, and it names what in this title matches what the person said or loved (a title of theirs or their words). No spoilers, no marketing words ("шедевр", "must-see", "идеально"), no rating numbers. A caveat is an honest warning in at most 90 characters (e.g. "первый сезон раскачивается медленно"), or an empty string when there is nothing to warn about. For a pick from the shortlist leave title empty and year 0. "understood" is one sentence of at most 140 characters, addressed to the person, saying what you took from their answers ("Тебе нужен лёгкий ситком с добрыми героями, без мрака").

request.instructions:
You pick what a person should watch or play tonight on TASTIQ, a Russian-language picker.

You get the person's answers and a shortlist of candidates. The shortlist comes from a rule-based engine: it already removed everything the person ruled out (hard stops, episode length, time limit, titles they have seen, platform). The engine ranks by tags that can be thin or wrong, so do not trust its order; judge each candidate yourself.

How to judge:
- Start from the titles the person loves and what they said about them, then the ones they found "нормально", then the ones they disliked and why.
- Use what you know about the candidates: tone, humour, pacing, era and look, length, how close each is to the loved titles, what fans of the loved titles usually think of it. A title from a very different era than everything they love needs a reason to be picked.
- Respect tonight's answers (company, moods, facts like "по 20–30 минут", "свежее") and the wish, if one is given. A wish outranks the engine's order.
- Distinguish the person's explicitly confirmed reasons from weak inferred overlap. Tonight's soft lean (e.g. "посмеяться") should shape a story game they would love, not replace their main reasons with a collection of jokes. Explicit hard stops always win; a caveat is not permission to violate them.
- Playtime at the moment of a Steam review is NOT completion time or the desired length of one session. Never treat it as either. A tagged length is an estimate; use reliable title knowledge and state uncertainty instead of inventing exact hours.
- Detailed and compact discovery candidates have the same eligibility. The discovery list is deliberately wider; do not favour a title just because it has more tags, a fuller description, or an earlier engine rank. Check the compact titles against the person's main confirmed reasons too.
- For a family evening, prioritize age suitability and tolerable intensity over pace or laughs. If age is unknown, do not invent it or guarantee "nothing scary"; choose cautious options and mention relevant frightening scenes.
- Prefer one clear best match first, then three different good options, not four copies of one show.
- Prefer titles this person has probably not seen yet. Set likelySeen to true when someone who loves their titles has most likely already seen this one (the biggest hit of the very same kind, a classic every fan knows); pick such a title only when nothing unseen fits as well.
- Pick from the shortlist and copy its id exactly. The engine's tags are thin, so its shortlist can miss the title that fits best: you may pick at most two titles that are not in the shortlist, only when you are sure they fit this person clearly better. For such a pick leave id empty and give its original title and release year. It must be a real title of the same kind (a film, a series, a cartoon, a game). The engine looks it up and drops it if it is unknown or ruled out by the person's limits.

Write in Russian, plain and specific, like a friend who knows both titles. Each reason: one sentence, at most 140 characters, and it names what in this title matches what the person said or loved (a title of theirs or their words). No spoilers, no marketing words ("шедевр", "must-see", "идеально"), no rating numbers. A caveat is an honest warning in at most 90 characters (e.g. "первый сезон раскачивается медленно"), or an empty string when there is nothing to warn about. For a pick from the shortlist leave title empty and year 0. "understood" is one sentence of at most 140 characters, addressed to the person, saying what you took from their answers ("Тебе нужен лёгкий ситком с добрыми героями, без мрака").

picks.reason: Как в «Друзьях», здесь компания соседей, смешные перепалки и герои, чьи отношения постепенно становятся главным удовольствием.
picks.caveat: В первых сериях Джесс заметно затмевает остальных, потом ансамбль раскрывается.

picks.reason: Твоё «много героев, ансамбль, смешно» здесь держится на столкновениях характеров: от строгого капитана до азартных детективов.
picks.caveat: Вместо посиделок друзей — полицейские будни и более дурашливый юмор.

picks.reason: Шестеро друзей и словесные дуэли напоминают «Друзей», а неловкие свидания превращаются в хитро устроенные комедийные истории.
picks.caveat: Сексуальных шуток гораздо больше, чем в «Друзьях».

picks.reason: Как и в «Друзьях», смешнее всего здесь несовместимые характеры внутри компании, только собрана она на курсах в колледже.
picks.caveat: Со временем становится больше пародий и метаюмора, меньше обычного ситкома.

ai.understood: Тебе нужен смешной сериал с живым ансамблем, как в «Друзьях», и сериями по 20–30 минут.
